subject: Request: Priority Response Corridor for LumenEdge — latency-floor exception
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Priority Response Corridor for LumenEdge — latency-floor exception

Team,

Quick context — LumenEdge (contact: Tom Harris) is a top-20 target with a likely $1.1M ARR profile in year 1 if we can meet their latency and throughput asks. They want a contractual "priority response corridor" covering their core inference path: embeddings + reranker for real-time personalization. Their ask (from our discovery call): P95 <= 75ms for single-turn generation/embeddings at baseline 2k qps with spikes to 8k qps during peak windows. They understand tradeoffs and said they prefer negotiating a carveout rather than walking.

Asking product/infra: is there a realistic plan to offer a documented SLA exception (short-term pilot) that guarantees sub-75ms P95 for that workload? If not exact, what is the nearest achievable commitment and what would we need (Dedicated capacity, zonal placement, reserved burst, model quantization, KV+prefix caching)? Also copying legal for any compliance indicators.

Attached: lumenedge_mrp_20270720.pdf (MRP / expected traffic profile).

Next steps I need:
- Product: feasibility + proposed configuration and ops burden (ETA for pilot start).
- SRE/ops: runbook requirements and monitoring obligations.
- Legal: pointers on wording we should avoid in the initial carveout.

Goal: get a interim proposal to LumenEdge by EOD Thu.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Priority Response Corridor for LumenEdge — latency-floor exception

Karthik — thanks for the detail and the MRP. High level response from product side:

1) Feasibility: technically possible for a pilot if LumenEdge is willing to:
   - Use a dedicated fleet (Reserved Dedicated pool on A100s or H100s depending on model)
   - Accept aggressive caching (prefix and KV) and a slightly quantized model variant for the production path.

2) Expected outcomes:
   - With Dedicated + optimized kernels and KV caching, P95 sub-75ms is reachable for embeddings + small-generation workloads at ~2k sustained qps.
   - Spikes to 8k qps will require burst capacity or autoscale with short warm-up; guaranteed 8k sustained at 75ms would be expensive and complex.

3) Tradeoffs / risk:
   - Increased unit cost (we should quantify uplift vs hosted baseline).
   - Operational burden: dedicated on-call escalation and a bespoke fallback policy (auto-fallback to a slightly higher-latency variant).

4) Requirements from sales/legal:
   - Precise traffic profile (qps distribution by hour) — MRP helps but we need 1-week of simulated trace.
   - Agreement on acceptable fallback behavior (e.g., 99.9% of requests must meet P95; exceptions during planned maintenance).

Proposed next step: product will draft a configuration proposal (Dedicated pool sizing, quantization level, cache policy, estimated cost uplift) and an initial runbook outline. I can get an initial config sketch by tomorrow EOD if SRE confirms resource availability.

cc: dev for early legal flags.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Product Lead, Serving Runtime
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@lumenedge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-26T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Priority Response Corridor for LumenEdge — latency-floor exception

Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Redwood is prepared to explore a timeboxed pilot that targets a guaranteed low-latency path for your personalization stack. Before we finalize the pilot proposal, a few asks to make sure we size things right:

1) Can you share a 7-day sample trace (or synthetic generator) with qps by minute and 95th percentile payload sizes?
2) What SLAs are must-haves vs nice-to-haves? You mentioned sub-75ms P95 for core embeddings — is that a hard requirement for the pilot or a negotiable target?
3) Procurement timeline: do you have an internal review window and an expected PO date?

We'll come back with a concrete Dedicated sizing proposal and a mutual action plan including milestones, monitoring dashboard access, and a draft SLA carveout.

I'll loop in Product & SRE internally so we can keep momentum.

— Karthik
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: se an_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-27T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Priority Response Corridor for LumenEdge — latency-floor exception

Karthik / Aditya — putting together an ops-first view. Short answers then a runbook stub attached.

Short: yes, we can run a priority corridor but it means:
- Dedicated pool with pinned GPUs in the same region as LumenEdge traffic (reduces variance).
- Pre-warm warmup windows and reserved burst capacity. For spike windows to ~8k qps we'll need a pre-provisioned burst layer or a policy that drops non-priority traffic.
- Strict isolation of KV/prefix cache to avoid eviction from other tenants.

Monitoring / SLOs:
- We'll expose a per-token latency dashboard and per-route P95 alarms.
- Need an escalation matrix (oncall + product owner) for sustained degradations.

Operational caveats (must be surfaced to the customer):
- Planned maintenance windows will be excluded from the carveout.
- Cost uplift will be material — suggest we be explicit about a peak inhalation policy to cap exposure.

Runbook attached: lumenedge_operational_runbook.md (contains playbook items, burn rate thresholds, rollback steps).

Quote from the runbook in case you forward to Tom:
"If P95 > 75ms for longer than 5m, escalate to SRE lead; if >15m, trigger auto-fallback to standard hosted model variant and open incident."

I'll join client call if we get to proposal stage.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
SRE Manager, Redwood Console
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-29T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA carveout & next steps for LumenEdge

Marissa / Karthik — attaching a redline of the SLA carveout and a short list of legal guardrails. Key points:

- Avoid absolute guarantees across "unbounded" traffic. Use timeboxed commitments and explicit exclusions (maintenance, DDOS, customer misconfiguration).
- Define fallback behavior and customer-visible messaging (we recommend an "active fallback" clause rather than silent degradation).
- Limit credits/caps for SLA breaches and specify remediation cadence.

Attachment: sla_term_draft_redlines.docx

If you want an exec-signed concession (outside standard T&Cs) we need a one-page risk memo for the Risk Committee. I can draft that if sales confirms they want to pursue.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-29T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA carveout & next steps for LumenEdge

Karthik / Marissa — thumbs up from Ops/Product. We can allocate the necessary Dedicated pool for a Q3 pilot provided sales commits a minimum 3-month reserved spend and LumenEdge signs the timeboxed carveout with the exclusions Dev outlined.

Ask Sales to confirm: expected start date and PO cadence so finance can pre-approve spending (we'll track this as a concession against the Q3 bookings target).

If you get confirmation from the customer, I'll schedule a short resource kickoff and assign an SRE lead.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
VP, Product Operations
